answer: Yes. `pull` shares and `uri:` pages never ask for sign-in and read the other space anonymously, so a public space (read set to **Public (not signed in)**) works. Pages are addressed as `<space url>/<page name>`, for example `https://example.com/notes/Shared/Page`. The memory doesn't describe a "URL prefix" setting by that name.

--- ADR/004 Federation.md ---
Context | Context
Users wanted to reference and read pages from *other* spaces, shared libraries, public/published spaces without copying the content into their own.

--- API/sbShare.md ---
Configuration
On a new device a space can be known (from `share.silverbullet.spaces`) without a usable credential on that device (none, or an expired one that can’t be refreshed). Before a `push` or `sync` share, the `share:ensure` service then asks `Sign in to <space>?` and runs the device flow, so a private space is never read anonymously first (with a usable credential it does nothing). Declining fails with `Not connected to <space>` and leaves the page and the remote alone. `pull` shares and `uri:` pages never ask: they read anonymously. For a URI of a space that is not known at all, `share:ensure` first finds the space root with `sbShare.findSpaceRoot` (for `http:` and `https:` URIs), asks `Connect to <space>?`, signs in and remembers the space.

--- Guide/Best Practices.md ---
Flat name space | Querying your space
Begin in [[Workbench/Data]] to inspect records and build filters. [[Guide/Add Structure and Query]] teaches this without handwritten syntax. When you adapt the source:

* Prefer `index.contentPages()` for ordinary page lists. It excludes [[Meta Page|meta pages]] such as library and configuration pages. Use `index.pages()` when you want those included.
* Choose the right kind: `index.tasks()` reads tasks. `index.contentPages()` reads pages. Both can be narrowed to a tag.
* Use the [[Guide/Aggregator Pages|aggregator pattern]] for collections that would otherwise need a second membership list.
* Inspect [[Aspiring Pages]] to find forward references that have not acquired content yet. Not every such link is a mistake.

[[Object Index]] owns the index helpers and user-visible behavior.

--- API/sbShare.md ---
Configuration
Helpers behind sharing pages to another SilverBullet space. See [[^Library/Std/Infrastructure/SilverBullet Share]] and [[API/share]].

A shared page is addressed by a URI of the form `<space url>/<page name>`, for example `https://example.com/notes/Shared/Page`. Reads and writes use the other space’s `.fs` API with a token obtained through the device flow, kept under the credential key `sb:<space url>` (see [[API/auth]]).

One `net.readURI:` / `net.writeURI:` service pair handles every space. Its `match` resolves the URI when it is dispatched, so it claims URIs of any space known at that moment (from `share.silverbullet.spaces` or a stored credential), including spaces configured after this page loaded. Its priority is above the generic `https:` reader.

--- Publishing.md ---
Make a space public | Make a space public
In the [[Dashboard]], open the space’s **Space settings → Access**. Under **Who has access**, set **Public (not signed in)** to **Read**. Anyone can now read the space without signing in. Page history and [[Revisions]] stay members-only.

Visitors get the full SilverBullet client, including navigation, [[Linked Mention|linked mentions]] and live [[Space Lua/Integrated Query|queries]], but can’t edit anything or reach capability endpoints such as the shell or the [[Runtime API]]. Members with `write` access keep editing as usual, and visitors see changes as soon as they’re saved. See [[Dashboard#Access]] for how public access combines with member roles.

Under **Space settings → General**, set **Index page** to choose the page visitors land on (see [[Index Page]]).
